page: Amazon Web Services m8gd.16xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Graviton processor family. Built on the 64-bit ARM64 architecture using ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 cores, this server features 64 dedicated physical cores running at 2.8 GHz with a 1:1 thread-to-core ratio. The hardware configuration includes 256 GB of system memory, providing 4 GB of RAM per core, and is equipped with 3,800 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps.

Benchmark data highlights top-tier performance in memory-intensive and multi-threaded operations. The instance achieves top 10% placement in memory bandwidth tests, reaching 7,392.89 GB/sec for cached read-only small blocks and 464.3 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Multi-threaded processing is highly efficient, with top-tier results in Geekbench multi-core scores, software compilation with Clang, and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression. Database operations and Redis SET operations also rank in the top 10%, processing 134.49 million operations per second. However, single-core performance and single-threaded text processing remain in the average tier.

Utilizing custom ARM-based Graviton processors allows the m8gd.16xlarge to offer high compute density and memory bandwidth with favorable qualitative cost efficiency compared to traditional x86 architectures. The combination of 64 dedicated physical cores, high-speed local NVMe SSD storage, and 30 Gbps network bandwidth makes this instance well-suited for high-throughput database workloads, Redis caching layers, static web serving, and multi-threaded software compilation pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services m8gd.16xlarge is a general-purpose, ARM64-based instance powered by 64 dedicated AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 physical cores running at 2.8 GHz. It features 256 GB of system memory and 3,800 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage, operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with a 30 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark results indicate top-tier performance in memory bandwidth, multi-core processing, software compilation, and database operations, with Redis SET operations achieving 134.49 million operations per second. While single-core performance is average, the instance's high core density and integrated local storage provide excellent qualitative cost efficiency for multi-threaded tasks. This server is highly suited for high-throughput databases, caching layers, static web serving, and CI/CD compilation workloads.
